_common: Use the reference storyboard sheet ONLY as look and colour reference. Create ONE single full-frame photorealistic 16:9 photograph, NOT a grid, NO panel numbers, NO text, NO UI, NO labels, NO logos. Full-frame camera, true colours, real textures, subtle film grain, not CGI, no plastic look. Modern German carpentry workshop reality, people in modern black slim workwear, no clichés (no carpenter hats, no guild clothing, no pipes, no rustic folklore). Every drawer front and door has at most one handle or is handleless.

AH1.p: (panel 1) A tall handleless walnut chest of seven drawers stands slightly left of centre in an empty dark bordeaux room (deep wine-red plaster walls #2a0f14, dark oak floor), lit by one soft warm spotlight from above; the top drawer is pulled out about 3 cm and warm golden light glows out of the gap. Generous empty dark space on the right for a headline. Eye-level, 50mm, calm and luxurious.

AH2.p: (panel 2) Straight top-down view into a wide solid walnut drawer pulled fully out on full-extension runners, the drawer is lined with dark anthracite felt; inside lie exactly five rectangular solid wood sample blocks of equal size in one row with even gaps, left to right: light oak, dark walnut, pale ash, reddish cherry, creamy maple, each showing its real grain. The lower third of the drawer is empty felt. Warm soft light.

AH3.p: (panel 3) Extreme macro photograph of the freshly planed end grain of a European oak block: clearly visible annual growth rings as arcs, large earlywood pores as tiny dark holes in rows, fine rays as thin light lines, warm side light, shallow depth of field at the edges, fills the whole frame. Real wood, not a 3D pattern.

AH4.p: (panel 4, left half) Top-down view into an open walnut drawer lined with dark felt: a black laser distance meter, a tablet showing a clean line drawing of a stair niche, and a pencil lying neatly side by side, warm soft light.

AH5.p: (panel 4, right half) In an empty renovated old German apartment a carpenter (about 30, short dark hair, black work clothes) stands in front of an empty sloped niche under a staircase, a green cross line laser on a small tripod projects a bright green horizontal and vertical line onto the bare plaster, he holds a tablet. Plain grey plaster, concrete floor, daylight from a window. BEFORE state, the niche is empty.

AH6.p: (panel 5) Low angle along the bed of a modern CNC nesting router in a carpentry workshop: the spindle with a transparent brush dust hood is cutting along a toolpath into a large light MDF board, already cut contour grooves of furniture parts visible on the board, dust sucked into the hose, warm workshop light, shallow depth of field.

AH7.p: Two carpenters in black work clothes and gloves lay a large bookmatched walnut veneer sheet onto a panel in front of an open heated veneer press (Furnierpresse) in a modern workshop, the press plates open above, warm light, the grain is beautiful.

AH8.p: (panel 7, right part) A young female apprentice (about 19, ponytail, safety glasses, black work clothes) feeds an oak-veneered panel into a modern edge banding machine (Kantenanleimmaschine), her trainer (about 45, black work clothes) stands beside her and watches, modern bright workshop.

AH9.p: (panel 6, left part) Top-down view into an open walnut drawer lined with dark felt: yellow-black ear defenders, clear safety glasses and four blank cream name badges (no text) arranged neatly, warm light.

AH10.p: (panel 6, right part) Group portrait of four young carpenters (two women, two men, 20-30) in matching black workwear standing relaxed and confident in a modern carpentry workshop with CNC machines and panel saw behind them, one with arms crossed, natural smiles, editorial, warm light, they stand in the right two thirds of the frame, empty space left.

AH11.p: (panel 7, left part) Top-down view into an open walnut drawer lined with dark felt with six blank cream cards laid in two rows (no text), warm light.

AH12.p: The finished built-in cabinet in the same sloped niche under the staircase of the renovated old apartment: handleless oak-veneered fronts follow the slope exactly, three full-extension drawers at the low end, perfect even shadow gaps, a carpenter kneels and checks a gap, daylight. AFTER state.

AK1.p: Product photo: a low modern sideboard with four handleless fronts on a slim black steel base, made of light European OAK with an oiled finish, standing in front of a dark bordeaux wall on a dark oak floor, soft warm spotlight, straight frontal view, centred, whole sideboard visible.

AK2.p: Edit the reference photograph: keep EVERYTHING exactly the same (camera, sideboard shape, base, wall, floor, light, position), change ONLY the wood of the sideboard to dark American WALNUT, oiled.

AK3.p: Edit the reference photograph: keep EVERYTHING exactly the same, change ONLY the wood of the sideboard to pale European ASH, oiled.

AK4.p: Edit the reference photograph: keep EVERYTHING exactly the same, change ONLY the wood of the sideboard to reddish European CHERRY, oiled.

AK5.p: Edit the reference photograph: keep EVERYTHING exactly the same, change ONLY the wood of the sideboard to creamy European MAPLE, oiled.

AC1.p: A female trainer (about 40) and a male apprentice (about 18) laugh together at a solid wood workbench in a modern carpentry workshop, he holds a freshly cut walnut drawer side, warm light, black workwear, natural candid moment, space on the left.

AW1.p: A modern timber store in a carpentry workshop: tall vertical racks with stacked solid hardwood boards (oak, walnut, ash, cherry, maple) separated by sticks, a carpenter in black workwear checks the moisture of a board with a pin-type wood moisture meter, warm light.

AP1.p: Customer consultation in the bright showroom corner of a carpentry workshop: a carpenter in black workwear and a young couple sit at a large oak table with wood samples, veneer swatches and a tablet showing a 3D drawing of a built-in cabinet, warm daylight, friendly.

AW2.p: Wide view of a modern clean carpentry workshop hall: CNC nesting router, sliding panel saw, edge banding machine, yellow dust extraction ducts along the ceiling, large skylights, two workers in black workwear in the distance, organised and bright, no clutter.

AL1.p: (panel 1) An empty solid wood workbench stands alone in the centre of a dark bordeaux stage under one warm spotlight, nothing on it, lots of dark space around, calm and promising.

AL2.p: (panel 2) Month 2: the apprentice marks rough sawn walnut boards with a pencil and a steel square on the workbench, a few hand tools neatly beside her, warm workshop light.

AL3.p: (panel 3) Month 8: the apprentice cuts a walnut board on a modern sliding panel saw (Formatkreissaege) with safety glasses and ear defenders, the saw guard and dust extraction hood visible, fine dust in the light.

AL4.p: (panel 4) Month 14: the apprentice holds a tablet next to a modern CNC router that is cutting the cabinet back panel, finished carcass parts with wooden dowels lie ready on a cart in front.

AL5.p: (panel 5) Month 20: the walnut cabinet carcass stands glued up in many parallel clamps on the workbench, the apprentice tightens the last clamp, glue squeeze-out visible at the joints.

AL6.p: (panel 6) Month 28: the apprentice lays out bookmatched walnut veneer leaves like an opened book on the table of a veneer press, the mirrored grain forms a symmetrical pattern.

AL7.p: (panel 7) Month 34: the apprentice wipes oil onto the finished walnut cabinet door with a cotton cloth, the grain glows deep and warm under the oil.

AL8.p: (panel 8) Month 36: the finished tall two-door walnut cabinet with bookmatched doors on slim black steel legs stands alone on the dark bordeaux stage under a spotlight, the young woman stands proudly beside it with crossed arms, smiling.

_common_L: Use the reference storyboard sheet ONLY as look and colour reference. Create ONE single full-frame photorealistic 16:9 photograph, NOT a grid, NO panel numbers, NO text, NO timeline, NO UI, NO labels, NO logos. Full-frame camera, true colours, real textures, subtle film grain, not CGI, no plastic look. Deep bordeaux and walnut colour world, warm spotlight light. The apprentice is always the SAME young woman (about 20, dark brown hair in a ponytail, black slim workwear, safety glasses when at machines). The piece she builds is always the SAME tall two-door cabinet in American walnut with bookmatched veneer doors on slim black steel legs. No clichés (no carpenter hats, no guild clothing).
